sections.content: How many people are "mining and quarry workers and related operatives"?

7,220 people

were counted on the census as "mining and quarry workers and related operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Quarry workers put up supports in underground workings, set and detonate explosives to loosen rocks, set up and operate drilling equipment to extract coal and other minerals from the ground, and operate machinery to wash, crush or separate stone and ores.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "mining and quarry workers and related operatives" there were more men than women (96.2% compared with 3.8%).

This means "mining and quarry workers and related operatives" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 96.2% and women made up 3.8% of "mining and quarry workers and related operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "mining and quarry workers and related operatives" included:

  • rail construction and maintenance operatives
  • metal machining setters and setter-operators
  • taxi and cab drivers and chauffeurs

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "mining and quarry workers and related operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "mining and quarry workers and related operatives", 13.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "mining and quarry workers and related operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "mining and quarry workers and related operatives" included:

  • mobile machine drivers and operatives (other)
  • other skilled trades
  • security guards and related occupations

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "mining and quarry workers and related operatives", 8.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (94.2% compared with 5.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90.5%) than self-employed (9.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the same region of the South West.
